content: This strategic procurement, reported in June 2026, highlights Sarens’ intent to bolster its heavy lifting capabilities, specifically aligning with the rigorous demands of the mining and heavy construction industries [3,4]. Such investments underscore a broader industry trend where large-scale operators focus on heavy lifting and rigging specializations to capture high-value contracts. This aligns seamlessly with the profile of large-scale market participants, identified as Competitor A in structural market analyses, which maintain extensive fleets of mobile cranes dedicated primarily to heavy lifting and complex rigging operations. Nevertheless, the period witnessed crucial growth in renewable energy capacity, particularly within wind and solar energy projects, which were significantly accelerated by the Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme (REIPPPP) [43] . This gradual but vital shift in the energy landscape has had a profound impact on ancillary industries, most notably the crane hire and heavy lifting sector. Such large-scale private investments invariably translate into sustained, long-term contracts for the crane hire industry, providing a buffer against the volatility of public sector procurement delays. Looking beyond the historical constraints, the current energy landscape as of June 2026 remains heavily shaped by these foundational developments, with forward-looking investments aiming to drastically accelerate renewable energy adoption and improve grid reliability .
